rules.summary: The fee for a sexual assault forensic exam may not be charged or billed to the survivor or to the survivor's insurance.
rules.quote: The fee for conducting an examination of a victim pursuant to this section shall not be charged or billed to the victim or to the victim's insurance carrier.
rules.pinpoint: K.S.A. 65-448(h) as amended by 2026 HB 2613, sec. 1

params.payer: Kansas Crime Victims Compensation Board (crime victims compensation fund)

rules.summary: For assaults in Kansas, the state Crime Victims Compensation program pays for sexual assault forensic exams starting July 1, 2026.
rules.quote: Effective July 1, 2026, sexual assault forensic examinations for assaults that occur in Kansas, are to be paid by Kansas Crime Victims Compensation.
rules.pinpoint: Kansas AG Crime Victims Compensation page, SAFE Program section

rules.summary: Payment of the exam fee does not depend on the survivor otherwise qualifying for a compensation award.
rules.quote: Payment of such fee is not contingent on a victim or claimant being otherwise eligible for compensation under K.S.A. 74-7301 et seq., and amendments thereto.

params.payer: Kansas Crime Victims Compensation Board (exam only, not treatment)

rules.summary: The exam payment covers the forensic exam only. Other medical treatment from the same visit is billed to the survivor or their insurance, and the survivor can apply for compensation for it.
rules.quote: The CVCB will only pay for the exam, not the medical treatment, of sexual assault victims.
rules.pinpoint: SAFE Program Reimbursement Invoice, Billing Instructions

rules.summary: All compensation paid for one victim's injury, to the victim and every other claimant combined, may not exceed $25,000.
rules.quote: Compensation payable to a victim and to all other claimants sustaining economic loss because of injury to or death of that victim may not exceed $25,000 in the aggregate.

rules.summary: Lost wages are paid at the actual loss or $800 per week, whichever is less.
rules.quote: Compensation for work loss, replacement services loss, dependent's economic loss and dependent's replacement service loss may not exceed $800 per week or actual loss, whichever is less.

rules.summary: Mental health counseling is covered up to $5,000; the board can approve more in extenuating circumstances.
rules.quote: Any victim of a crime may be considered for up to a $5,000 mental health counseling award.

rules.summary: Outpatient individual or family counseling in a nonmedical setting is paid at up to $90 per hour.
rules.quote: Individual and family mental health counseling in a nonmedical setting $90 per hour

rules.summary: Group therapy is paid at up to $60 per hour.
rules.quote: Group therapy $60 per hour

rules.summary: Crime scene cleanup is covered up to $2,500.
rules.quote: "Allowance expense" includes a total charge not in excess of $2,500 for expenses in any way related to crime scene cleanup.

rules.summary: Funeral, cremation or burial expenses are covered up to $7,500.
rules.quote: "Allowance expense" includes a total charge not in excess of $7,500 for expenses in any way related to funeral, cremation or burial

rules.summary: Reasonable medical care, mental health counseling and other services needed because of the injury are covered.
rules.quote: This includes reasonable medical care, mental health counseling or other services necessary as a result of the injury.
rules.pinpoint: Kansas AG Crime Victims Compensation page, overview

rules.summary: Mileage for medically necessary travel can be covered, at no more than the state mileage rate.
rules.quote: Mileage costs may be deemed allowable expenses for medically necessary travel.

rules.summary: Moving costs can be covered when a law enforcement officer, a prosecutor, or a victim advocate at a law enforcement agency or prosecutor's office recommends the move in writing for reasons related to the crime.
rules.quote: Moving costs may be deemed allowable expenses if one of the following individuals has recommended the move in writing for reasons related to the crime: (1) A law enforcement officer; (2) a prosecutor; or (3) a victims' advocate working for a law enforcement agency or prosecutor's office.

rules.summary: Reasonable costs to replace clothing and bedding seized as evidence are covered.
rules.quote: Reasonable costs for replacement of clothing and bedding seized as evidence are compensable.

params.item: personal property loss (for example a phone), except clothing and bedding seized as evidence or property removed during crime scene cleanup

rules.summary: Lost or damaged personal property, such as a phone, is not covered. The exceptions are clothing and bedding seized as evidence and property removed during crime scene cleanup.
rules.quote: Personal property loss is not covered, with the exception of clothing and bedding seized as evidence, or property that had to be removed during the crime scene clean-up process.
rules.pinpoint: Kansas AG Crime Victims Compensation page, overview

params.item: pain and suffering; other property loss and property damage

rules.summary: Pain and suffering, and property loss or damage other than the listed exceptions, are not paid.
rules.quote: Other property loss, property damage and pain and suffering are ineligible expenses.

rules.summary: Meal costs are not covered.
rules.quote: Meal costs shall not be deemed allowable expenses.

params.extension: Two years from notice of a DNA match to a suspect or of a suspect's identification; the longest applicable limit applies (74-7305(b)(3)); the board may also award if denial would be a severe injustice (74-7305(b)(2)(D)).

rules.summary: Most claims must be filed within five years of the injury. If a survivor is told that DNA testing of a sexual assault kit or other evidence matched a suspect, or that a suspect was identified, they have two years from that notice. The longest deadline that applies is the one that counts, and the board can also accept a late claim if denying it would be a severe injustice.
rules.quote: (A) The claim has been filed with the division within five years after the injury or death upon which the claim is based; (B) in a case where a victim who is notified that DNA testing of a sexual assault kit or other evidence has revealed a DNA profile of a suspected offender who victimized the victim or the victim on whose behalf the claim is made, or is notified of the identification of a suspected offender who victimized the victim or the victim on whose behalf the claim is made, the claim has been filed with the division within two years of such notification

rules.summary: For a sexually violent crime, the board may accept a claim filed within 10 years after the crime. "Sexually violent crime" is a defined list in K.S.A. 22-3717 that includes rape and aggravated sexual battery but not every sexual offense.
rules.quote: a victim of a sexually violent crime as defined in K.S.A. 22-3717, and amendments thereto, if: (a) The claim has been filed with the division within 10 years after the date such crime was committed

rules.summary: If the survivor of a sexually violent crime was under 18 when it happened, the claim can be filed up to 10 years after they turn 18.
rules.quote: the victim was less than 18 years of age at the time such crime was committed, and the claim has been filed within 10 years after the date the victim turns 18 years of age

params.extension: If more than one limit applies, the longest one applies (74-7305(b)(3)).

rules.summary: When the victim was under 16 and the crime was a sexually violent crime or certain trafficking or enticement crimes, the claim is due within two years of the report to law enforcement, unless a longer limit also applies.
rules.quote: Compensation may not be awarded unless an application has been filed with the division within two years of the reporting of the incident to law enforcement officials if the victim was less than 16 years of age

rules.summary: To qualify, the crime must be reported to law enforcement within 72 hours, OR the survivor must have had a forensic medical exam within seven days, OR the board must find good cause for missing both.
rules.quote: Compensation may not be awarded unless: (1) The criminally injurious conduct resulting in injury or death was reported to a law enforcement officer within 72 hours after the occurrence of the criminally injurious conduct; (2) the victim obtained a forensic medical examination within seven days after the occurrence of the criminally injurious conduct; or (3) the board finds there was good cause for the failure to report or obtain an examination within the time limits provided in this subsection.

rules.summary: The board must pay the forensic exam fee even if the survivor chooses not to report the assault to law enforcement.
rules.quote: refusal of the victim to report the alleged offense to law enforcement shall not excuse
rules.pinpoint: K.S.A. 65-448(h) as amended by 2026 HB 2613, sec. 1

rules.summary: The board can deny, withdraw or reduce an award if the claimant or victim did not fully cooperate with law enforcement.
rules.quote: The board, upon finding that the claimant or victim has not fully cooperated with appropriate law enforcement agencies, may deny, withdraw or reduce an award of compensation.

rules.summary: Compensation is reduced by anything already recovered from other sources, such as insurance.
rules.quote: Economic loss upon which the claimant's claim is based is recouped from other persons, including collateral sources

rules.summary: The board may reduce or deny an award for the claimant's or victim's contributory misconduct.
rules.quote: board deems reasonable because of the contributory misconduct of the claimant or of a victim through whom the claimant claims

rules.summary: The reduction for a victim likely engaging in unlawful activity at the time of the crime may not be used against victims of domestic abuse or sexual assault.
rules.quote: The provisions of subsection (d)(1)(C) shall not be construed to reduce or deny compensation to a victim of domestic abuse or sexual assault.

rules.summary: If the claimant would face financial hardship and a final award looks likely, the board may pay a tentative award that is later deducted from the final award.
rules.quote: If the board determines that the claimant will suffer financial hardship unless a tentative award is made, and it appears likely that a final award will be made, an amount may be paid to the claimant and shall be deducted from the final award

rules.summary: Adult sexual assault is a listed crime type on the state compensation application.
rules.quote: Sexual Assault (Adult)

params.rule: Crime occurred in Kansas; or Kansas domiciliary victimized in a U.S. state or territory with no eligible compensation program; or Kansas domiciliary victimized outside the United States (74-7301(e)(2)).

rules.summary: Crimes that happen in Kansas are covered. A Kansas resident hurt by a violent crime in another U.S. state or territory can apply only if that place has no eligible compensation program and the crime would be covered in Kansas.
rules.quote: Occurs or is attempted in this state or occurs to a person whose domicile is in Kansas who is the victim of a violent crime which occurs in another state, possession, or territory of the United States of America may make an application for compensation if: (i) The crimes would be compensable had it occurred in the state of Kansas; and (ii) the places the crimes occurred are states, possessions or territories of the United States of America not having eligible crime victim compensation programs

params.rule: Kansas domiciliary victimized outside the United States

rules.summary: A violent crime committed outside the United States against a Kansas resident can also qualify.
rules.quote: a violent crime that posed a substantial threat or caused personal injury or death, committed outside of the United States against a person whose domicile is in Kansas

not_found: expense_cap:transportation (rate set by reference to the state mileage rate, no dollar figure in the regulation)
coverage.notes: No minimum-loss threshold was found. Instead K.S.A. 74-7305(e) requires the board to find financial stress (the claimant cannot keep their customary level of health, safety and education without undue financial hardship), judged on dependents, living expenses, special needs, income, resources and other factors. Moving costs are allowed by K.A.R. 20-2-9(b) but no dollar cap was found. No security-measure coverage was found. Inpatient mental health care is capped per instance at 10 days or $10,000, whichever is less (K.A.R. 20-2-3(e)); not encoded because the schema has no per-instance unit. The application says unpaid medical bills assigned to a provider are paid at 80% of allowable charges as payment in full. A mental health evaluation is paid up to $350 on top of the $5,000 counseling limit (K.A.R. 20-2-3(a)(3)); not encoded as a separate cap.

researcher_notes: The compiled K.S.A. 65-448(h) on the legislature site (KS-S7) still says the county pays the exam fee, but the page flags 2026 HB 2613 as an enacted measure affecting the section. The enrolled HB 2613 (KS-S8) moves the fee to the Crime Victims Compensation Board, and the AG page (KS-S1) and SAFE invoice (KS-S3) say the program pays for exams from July 1, 2026. The rules use the newer law for the payer; the no-billing sentence is the same in both versions. The enrolled-bill PDF text mixes struck and inserted words, so quotes from it are limited to new text that reads cleanly. K.A.R. 20-2-6 (1993) still lists only a 72-hour police report; it was not used because the later statute, K.S.A. 74-7305(f), adds the forensic exam alternative. The ten-year deadline in 74-7305(b)(2)(C)(ii) applies to a 'sexually violent crime as defined in K.S.A. 22-3717'. Reviewer fetched 22-3717 (KS-S11): (d)(5) lists rape (21-5503), aggravated criminal sodomy, criminal sodomy under 21-5504(a)(3)-(4) only, aggravated sexual battery (21-5505(b)), child sex offenses, aggravated incest and attempts. Plain sexual battery (21-5505(a)) is not on the list, so those survivors get the general five-year limit. The SAFE invoice also tells providers survivors may apply whether or not they report to law enforcement. The OVC state directory lists the same phone (785-296-2359) and website. Reviewer: the 74-7301 page (KS-S5) lists 2026 HB 2780 (terramation) as an enacted measure affecting that section; it likely touches the funeral wording in 74-7301(a), and the amended text was not fetched, so KS-CAP-7 reflects the compiled pre-amendment text. The no-billing rule now cites the enrolled HB 2613 text (KS-S8) instead of the superseded compiled 65-448 (KS-S7); the sentence is identical. How to file: the application (KS-S2, revised May 2025, the version linked from the board page) has 202 fillable AcroForm fields but no mail-to address, online portal, email or fax instruction. The only filing destination in the official sources is the Contact block on the board page (KS-S1), so KS-SUBMIT-1 uses that mailing address. The same block lists a fax number, (785) 296-0652, and a generic 'Send us an email' form; neither is stated as a way to file an application, so no fax or email submission rule was added. The SAFE invoice (KS-S3) also lists that fax, but its submission instructions are for exam providers, not survivors. No online application was found. No photo ID or police report copy is requested; the form asks only for the police report number.
